statement: Conditioning first on the heavy-isotropic leakage projection T and replacing each conditional (Y,Z) law by its L-infinity density cap cannot give a universal QFORM bound. The exact coarea reduction pays J=integral p_T(t)^(1/3) m(t)^(2/3) dt, m(t)=ess sup_(y,z) g(t,y,z). A valid exact-rank-three Parseval target frame with eigenvalues {1,1,-1} and fragmented cap-one product inputs has J >= (N-1)/(6N)^(1/3), while the assigned-partner reverse mixed norm sup_(y,z) integral g(t,y,z)dt=||p_(Y,Z)||_infinity remains <=e.
scope: This refutes only the conditional-slice-sup closure mechanism, not the QFORM conjecture. A successful proof must keep the leakage variable inside the curved integration, or otherwise use stronger product-fiber provenance before taking slice suprema.
